What is it like to foster a kitten?

It depends. A feral kitten will take socializing, not for beginners. A kiitten under 6 weeks will require bottle feeding sometimes throughout the night. After six weeks you have 4 weeks to get it adopted before people lose interest in its size and you then become a proud owner. A happy owner too because you inevitably fall in love with all of them. I have fostered dozens and ended up with at least one a year. They are a tax write off you you keep them as foster status- don't outright adopt. My 2 cents, anyway.

We were foster folk's & here is our tale ( tail ) . I thought we should adopt 2 kits- siblings perhaps but not a big deal. Went to all the shelters & it was the off season & kittens were not to be found. Animal shelter said hey you can be a foster folk & help us out & if you like the kittens you have first dibs. Okay , that sounded good. So a couple weeks went by- my cell rang at work. We have a PG mom dumped off & she is giving birth right now. Would you like to see her? So after work I went to see her- she was in the middle of birth but did stop to acknowledge me. I found out she was a mix manx & balinese. She had a marmalade manx & 2 white longhairs. They said she really had another marm but was deformed & they put it down. She was eager to share her new kits with me & was such a sweet Mom. The shelter said they wanted to release her to me the next day & wanted to just observe her overnight. The next day I had a box for her & put in her kits & she jumped in & we drove to the house. Got to the house & had a litter box set up in back room & gave her 2 choices of rooms- I put her kits at the end of the hall & left her alone. She came into the Kitchen later & I showed her food & water & then showed her the cat door to the garage. No response so I shoved her through.- then on the kitty door to the outside- she just split. So her being outside I had 2 ooms to see if I could locate the 3 kits. Under the dresser! I could see them way in the back but no noise. So Rick came home- where are the kittens& the Mom? I said she was feeding them. She was a very nice kitty- trusting - a good Mom. But she did like her outside time- would come waltzing back in & then check on her kits. After a week Rick asked if she really had kits as he had not seen nor heard them. I told him yes but they had to be quiet because in the wild they would be killed by even making a noise if another tom found them. Then a couple days later at about 2ish in the morning I heard a squeak- I heard her meow walking on the bed- she left & we heard another squeak- she was bringing her kits to introduce them to us- in Bed!!! So she got all the kits on the bed & curled up between us & we all went back to sleep & woke up to squeaking & purring , We had her 3 more weeks & turned the Mom & 1 white kit back into the shelter & kept the boy white kitty Stumpy & the manx Garlick. We had them for 12 years- greatly loved & they ran the house. Do it !!!!

Forgive me, because I'm going to go outside the scope of your question and how it applies to just Nebraska/Omaha.

I've always been for the death penalty. I understand the arguments of the anti death penalty side, and I struggle with those arguments because many of them are valid, but ultimately, I think there should be and needs to be an ultimate punishment for an ultimate crime... we're not debating amputation of a hand for shoplifting, we are debating taking a life in response to maliciously taking a life. And despite a myriad of other issues with them, there is no group which could be considered more impartial to apply it than our government.

What I do think needs to change are the circumstances under which it is applied - the number of people executed and later being found to be innocent is far too high... anything greater than zero is too high. Perhaps the penalty could be applied only in circumstances in which there are multiple eyewitnesses, or independent, impartial evidence such as video... a simple conviction should not be enough given the clear corruption in many prosecutor's offices around the country.

There has been a lot of talk about the 8th Amendment implications of execution, and especially the manner in which it is performed. I disagree that any of the methods which have been used by the states over the years... electric chair, gas chamber, firing squads, hanging, and most especially lethal injection... are cruel and unusual, and in many particularly heinous cases, it is far less than what the condemned deserves. Recently, there have been discussions and lawsuits about the use of the drugs pentobarbital and midazolam. As someone who uses those drugs in my own work, I can say absolutely that when used in the proper amounts, they are more than sufficient to do the job, and to do it quickly and painlessly.

Regarding here in Nebraska specifically, I am shocked that a state that is as ideologically conservative as Nebraska would have such staunch opposition to the death penalty. I think we should continue to have it as an option and I think it should be simplified to the point of taking the condemned out back and shooting them in the back of the head. It should be applied sparingly and with the most careful consideration towards justice... and then it should be applied without mercy to those who have proven themselves to be without mercy.

GIANTS AND TOYS (1958) Director, Yasuzo Masumura

Giants and Toys is a 1958 Japanese comedy film directed by Yasuzo Masumura and starring Hiroshi Kawaguchi. It portrays the increasingly frenzied efforts of the World candy company to compete with the rival Giant and Apollo companies over caramel sales. World "discovers" a tomboy girl with bad teeth to be the center of their promotional campaign, involving colorful space suits and ray guns. The film satirizes the instant manufacture of media stars, the decline of a gentlemanly business ethos and rise of a culture of ruthless corporate skullduggery, and the emphasis on work at the expense of personal life and health.
